questions.enonce_markdown:
Computers in a network are linked by transmission media.

(a) Give two advantages and one disadvantage of fiber optic cable. (3 marks)

(b) Explain the concept of multiplexing. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Fibre optic cable (3 marks).**

*Two advantages* (any two):

- Very high bandwidth: data are sent at very high speed (many Gbit/s).
- Immune to electromagnetic interference and crosstalk, because light is used instead of electricity.
- Very low signal loss, so it covers long distances without repeaters.
- Difficult to tap, so the data are more secure; it is also thin and light.

*One disadvantage* (any one): the cable and its connection equipment are expensive; it is difficult to install and to join (it needs skilled technicians and special tools); and the glass fibre is fragile and cannot be bent sharply.

**(b) Multiplexing (2 marks).** Multiplexing is the technique of combining the signals from several sources into a single signal sent at the same time over one communication channel (cable or link) by a multiplexer; at the other end a demultiplexer separates them again and delivers each to its destination. It makes better use of the bandwidth of an expensive channel and reduces the number of cables needed. The main forms are frequency-division (FDM), time-division (TDM) and wavelength-division (WDM) multiplexing.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Consider the algorithm below

```
Line 1  start
Line 2  Get three numbers a, b, c
Line 3  Compute a*b + c
Line 4  Multiply the result of Line 3 by 10
Line 5  Store the result of Line 4 in Y
Line 6  Display Y
Line 7  Stop
```

(a) What is an algorithm? (2 marks)

(b) Give two parameters that are used to determine the efficiency an algorithm. (2 marks)

(c) What is the type of algorithm used above? (1 mark)

(d) Draw the flowchat for the algorithm. (3 marks)

(e) Name the type of control structure used in this algorithm. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The algorithm computes $Y = 10 \times (a \times b + c)$. For example, with $a = 2$, $b = 3$, $c = 4$: $2 \times 3 + 4 = 10$, then $10 \times 10 = 100$, so $Y = 100$ (checked by running the steps in a Python translation).

**(a) Algorithm (2 marks).** A finite, ordered set of clear and unambiguous steps (instructions) that, when followed, solves a problem or performs a task and ends after a limited number of steps, for given input data and giving an output.

**(b) Two parameters of efficiency (2 marks).** *Time complexity* (the running time, or number of steps executed, as the size of the input grows) and *space complexity* (the amount of memory the algorithm needs). (The number of operations and the simplicity of the steps are also accepted.)

**(c) Type of algorithm (1 mark).** A *sequential (linear) algorithm*, written in pseudocode (structured English): the steps are executed once, one after the other, with no decision and no repetition.

**(d) Flowchart (3 marks).** Terminators are ovals, input and output are parallelograms, and processes are rectangles:

```
        ( Start )
            |
            v
     /  Get a, b, c  /
            |
            v
    [ R = a * b + c ]
            |
            v
    [ Y = R * 10 ]
            |
            v
     /  Display Y  /
            |
            v
        ( Stop )
```

**(e) Control structure (1 mark).** **Sequence** (sequential structure): the instructions are executed in the order in which they are written.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give one function of each of the following processor components:

(a) ALU. (1 mark)

(b) Registers. (1 mark)

(c) Cache. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) ALU, Arithmetic and Logic Unit (1 mark).** It carries out the arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and the logical operations (AND, OR, NOT) and comparisons on the data.

**(b) Registers (1 mark).** Very small and very fast storage locations inside the CPU that temporarily hold the data, instructions, addresses and results being processed at the moment (for example the program counter and the accumulator).

**(c) Cache (1 mark).** A small, very fast memory placed between the CPU and the main memory that keeps copies of the instructions and data most recently or most often used, so the CPU can obtain them faster and waits less for the slower RAM.
